'''Bondy''' ({{IPA|fr|bɔ̃di|audio=Fr-Bondy.ogg}}) is a [[Communes of France|commune]] in the northeastern suburbs of Paris, France. It is located {{convert|10.9|km|mi|abbr=on}} from the [[Kilometre zero|centre]] of Paris, in the [[Seine-Saint-Denis]] [[Departments of France|department]].

==Name==
The name Bondy was recorded for the first time around AD 600 as ''Bonitiacum'', meaning "estate of Bonitius", a [[Gallo-Roman]] landowner.{{cn|date=November 2025}}

==History==
[[File:Forêt de Bondy carte de Cassini2.jpg|thumb|Bondy, c. 1780]]
[[File:Hôtel Ville Bondy 2.jpg|thumb|The [[Hôtel de Ville, Bondy|Hôtel de Ville]]]]
During the [[Middle Ages]], Bondy was mostly forest, and the forest of Bondy was a well-known haunt of bandits and robbers and was considered extremely dangerous.{{cn|date=November 2025}}

On January 3, 1905, a third of the territory of Bondy was detached and became the commune of [[Les Pavillons-sous-Bois]].{{cn|date=November 2025}}

The current [[Hôtel de Ville, Bondy|Hôtel de Ville]] was completed in 1970.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.histoiredebondy.fr/construction-de-lhotel-de-ville/   |title=La construction de l'Hôtel de Ville|publisher=Bondy son Chêne et ses Racines|access-date=April 15, 2025}}</ref>

On October 30, 2007, a gas explosion killed one person and injured 46 people.{{cn|date=November 2025}}

Bondy and its integration into Paris is the subject of part of the second-last chapter of [[Graham Robb]]'s book ''[[Parisians (book)|Parisians]]''.

==Administration==
Bondy is part of the [[canton of Bondy]], created in 2015.

==Transport==
Bondy is served by [[Bondy (Paris RER)|Bondy]] station on Paris [[RER E|RER line E]] and the [[Île-de-France tramway Line 4|Line 4 (T4) of the Tramways in Île-de-France]].

==Education==
{{As of|2016}}, the commune had 27 state-funded primary schools, with 6,900 students. There were also three publicly funded [[lycée]]s, or senior high schools, and five junior high schools.<ref>[http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/ "Vie scolaire"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160908002243/http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/ |date=September 8, 2016 }}. Bondy. Retrieved on September 6, 2016.</ref>
* There are 13 ''écoles maternelles'', or preschools,<ref>"[http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-ecoles-maternelles/ Les écoles maternelles] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916081349/http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-ecoles-maternelles/ |date=2016-09-16 }}." Bondy. Retrieved on September 6, 2016.</ref> and 14 publicly funded elementary schools<ref>"[http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-ecoles-elementaires/ Les écoles élémentaires] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916072555/http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-ecoles-elementaires/ |date=2016-09-16 }}." Bondy. Retrieved on September 6, 2016.</ref>
* The junior high schools are named after: Pierre Brossolette, Henri Sellier, Jean Zay, Jean Renoir, and Pierre Curie<ref>"[http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-colleges/ 60 millions d’euros pour les collèges] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916070052/http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-colleges/ |date=2016-09-16 }}." Bondy. Retrieved on September 6, 2016.</ref>
* There are three state-funded high schools: Lycée Léo-Lagrange, Lycée Marcel-Pagnol, and Lycée Jean-Renoir.<ref name=HS>"[http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-lycees/ Les lycées] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916071912/http://www.ville-bondy.fr/education/vie-scolaire/les-lycees/ |date=2016-09-16 }}." Bondy. Retrieved on September 6, 2016.</ref>

Bondy also has a private Roman Catholic high school, Institut privé de l'Assomption, which has its own elementary school.<ref name=HS/>
